frameworks.name: comparative_advantage
frameworks.notes: France's RCA in wine (HS 2204) is among the highest of any country-product pair in world trade. Terroir/branding make this quasi-Ricardian: fixed natural endowment (climate, land) = classic Ricardo.

frameworks.name: gravity
frameworks.notes: Wine trade highly sensitive to distance (bulk/shipping costs) and cultural proximity (francophonie, religion — alcohol demand). Use cultural distance explicitly.

products.name: wine
products.notes: Still wine from fresh grapes. Beware: many candidate markets (Muslim-majority) have near-zero alcohol demand — gravity score should penalize cultural distance, else scoring will produce absurd recommendations like exporting wine to Saudi Arabia.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: Fastest-growing wine market in SE Asia, young middle class, historical French colonial wine culture — cultural gravity favorable. French exports exist but small relative to market growth.

countries.name: India
countries.notes: Huge gravity pull, wine consumption tiny but rising; 150%+ import tariffs a major barrier; states vary in alcohol policy.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.notes: Large francophone-adjacent West African market, wine (often sweet/sparkling) demand exists; verify constraint.

trade_links.source: estimate — may FAIL $10M constraint; verify against Eurostat Comext. If it fails, note this is a 'recently-maturing' link and discuss with professor whether growth-stage links count as 'new'
